p: we will not ride upon horses;
and we will no longer say 'our god'
to the work of our hands, etc." (Hoshea 14:4).
that can happen to a person
it is in the power of each one
to return and draw near to the root
עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁלֹשֶׁת הָאָבוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים.
through the holiness of the three holy Avos.
this alludes to one who has fallen
into the depths of the kelipos of heresy and denial,
עִם כָּל זֶה יֵשׁ תִּקְוָה עוֹד לָשׁוּב,
even so there is still hope to return,
"And those lost in the land of Ashur will come."
who did not take part in the counsel of the generation of the Dispersion,
For the counsel of the generation of the Dispersion
was for the sake of avodah zarah,
who are "one nation in the land."
וְכֵן בְּאָמְרָם נִבְנֶה לָנוּ עִיר וּמִגְדָּל
And likewise in saying, "Let us build ourselves a city and a tower,"
הָיָה כַּוּוֹנָתָם נֶגֶד בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
their intent was against the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
מִצַּד שֶׁהָיָה כּוֹפֵר בְּכָל מִינֵי אֱלָהוּת.
because he denied every kind of divinity.
And it is brought in Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu (Rabbah 20)
that in reward for Ashur's separating from them,
כִּי זֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן כּוֹחוֹ שֶׁל סַנְחֵרִב,
For this was also the power of Sancheirev,
"Who among all the gods of the lands
that He should save Yerushalayim, etc.";
whereas all the nations call Him
And "those lost in the land of Ashur"
who were assimilated among the nations
through Sancheirev, who ruled over them
and brought into them the aspect of heresy;
HaKadosh Baruch Hu wished to make
Sancheirev into Gog and Magog and Chizkiyah into Mashiach.
כִּי זֶהוּ עִיקַּר קְלִיפַּת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג
For this is the essence of the kelipah of Gog and Magog,
זֶה לְעוּמַּת זֶה נֶגֶד מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד,
the opposite of Mashiach ben David,
"The kings of the earth stand up
against Hashem and against His anointed, etc.";
and it is the aspect of heresy.
And as we heard from our holy Rebbe of Izhbitz,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
zecher tzaddik livrachah l'chayei Olam HaBa,
שֶׁמִּזְּמַן הִתְגַּלּוּת עֵסֶק הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּעוֹלָם
that from the time the work of the holy Baal Shem Tov was revealed in the world,
this is a glimmering of the aspect of Mashiach;
רַק בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר יֵשׁ בַּקְּלִיפָּה
only that in every generation there is in the kelipah,
זֶה לְעוּמַּת זֶה, מִבְּחִינַת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג,
as its opposite, something of the aspect of Gog and Magog,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְרַבָּה הַמִּינוּת בָּעוֹלָם.
and through this heresy has increased in the world.
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ הַפָּסוּק אַשּׁוּר לֹא יוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ,
And this is the meaning of the pasuk "Ashur will not save us":
that there is hope to return to holiness
even from this fall into the aspect of heresy.
And it is through the power of the merit
who rooted in us the power of emunah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית טו, ו) וְהֶאֱמִין בַּה׳,
as it says (Bereishis 15:6), "And he believed in Hashem,"
"And the righteous one shall live by his faith";
that exists inwardly in the souls of Yisrael,
to revive itself from the pit.
And as the holy Ramban said
regarding why it does not say
the first Dibbur, "I am Hashem your God,"
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר שֶׁתָּלוּי בֶּאֱמוּנַת הַלֵּב,
because it is something that depends on the faith of the heart,
and if one does not believe,
רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּיבּוּר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
Rather, through Hashem Yisbarach's speaking to Yisrael
in the heart of Bnei Yisrael, that they believe,
so that they are believers, the children of believers.
וְגַם מִזֶּה יֵשׁ בְּכֹחַ כָּל אֶחָד
and from this too it is in the power of each one
as it is written, "And they will come, etc.,
and those cast away in the land of Mitzrayim,"
which alludes to the lust for immorality.
כִּי מִצְרַיִם נִקְרָא עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מב, ט),
For Mitzrayim is called "the nakedness of the land" (Bereishis 42:9),
and it is said of them (Yechezkel 23:20),
"and their issue is like the issue of horses,"
וּמוֹצָא הַסּוּסִים מִמִּצְרָיִם (מְלָכִים א י, כח),
and "the horses were brought out of Mitzrayim" (Melachim I 10:28),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים קיג, ב).
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד, יב, א):
And so they said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12:1):
and all the women were fenced off from immorality in her merit;
Yosef went down to Mitzrayim, etc.,
and all the males were fenced off in his merit."
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַפָּסוּק עַל סוּס לֹא נִרְכָּב,
And this is what the pasuk says, "We will not ride upon horses":
that a Jewish soul has the ability
to emerge even from this fall.
And it is through the power
שֶׁהִשְׁרִישׁ בָּנוּ יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
that Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom, rooted in us,
"And he dwelt in the land of the Negev,"
for his heart was dried out
of every desire and craving of this world.
וְלֹא נֹאמַר עוֹד אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵינוּ
"And we will no longer say 'our god' to the work of our hands"
corresponds to one who has fallen
into the state of forgetfulness and concealment
in the affairs of this world,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כּוֹחוֹ וְעוֹצֶם יָדוֹ יַעֲשֶׂה חָיִל.
that by his own strength and the might of his hand he will achieve success.
And about this it is said,
וְלֹא נֹאמַר עוֹד אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵינוּ,
"And we will no longer say 'our god' to the work of our hands":
שֶׁיּוּכַל גַּם מִזֶּה לַחֲזוֹר לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה
that even from this one can return to the root of holiness
עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
through the aspect of Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
from my beginning until this day";
שֶׁהָיְתָה מִדָּתוֹ בְּחִינַת אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב (מִיכָה ז, כ),
for his trait was the aspect of "truth to Yaakov" (Michah 7:20),
that he knew in his soul
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם כֹּחַ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו
that he had no power at all in the work of his hands
without the help of Hashem Yisbarach.
And although he said to Lavan (Bereishis 31:42),
"God has seen the toil of my hands,"
and as is brought in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 74:12):
"Great is the toil of one's hands,
which stood by Yaakov to save lives" —
עִם כָּל זֶה יָדַע בֶּטַח בְּנַפְשׁוֹ
nevertheless he knew with certainty in his soul
that he had no power at all in his deeds,
רַק מַה שֶּׁיַּסְכִּים הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָלָיו
only what Hashem Yisbarach would agree to for him
"I have become small through all the kindnesses and all the truth
that You have done for Your servant."
And as we heard from our holy Rebbe of Izhbitz,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
zecher tzaddik v'kadosh livrachah l'chayei Olam HaBa,
one who has a desire for holiness —
there is still no clarification in this.
even one in whom there is
even one in whom there is fervor
for the matter and occupation of avodah in holiness —
גַּם כֵּן אֵין עוֹד בֵּירוּר בְּכָל אֵלֶּה.
in all these too there is still no clarification.
רַק אַחֲרֵי הָאֵשׁ קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה:
Only "after the fire, a still, small voice":
are the signature of the hand of Hashem Yisbarach
found in the souls of Yisrael —
and then one can trust in the Name of Hashem,
but with nothing at all from his own side.
וְזֶהוּ וְלֹא נֹאמַר עוֹד אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵינוּ,
And this is "And we will no longer say 'our god' to the work of our hands,"
but rather "for in You the orphan finds compassion."
